# Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
          # gh-812: the builder reads the previous release's shipped catalog
          # and same-version pack zips (version uniqueness + payload compare).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # gh-812 rework (review thread 3): untrusted tag names reach the
          # script ONLY through env indirection — never template-expanded
          # into the run: block. Actions interpolates ${{ }} BEFORE bash
          # parses the script, so a crafted agents-rel-* tag name (any user
          # with push access can create one; the newest by creatordate wins)
          # could break out of the quoting and run arbitrary code in this
          # contents:write job.
          BASE_REF: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
          PREV_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-812 rework: release-base tags are machine-generated
          # (agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS); anything else in the newest
          # agents-rel-* tag is rejected before it reaches the builder.
          # Empty is allowed — the first release has no base tag.
          for tag in "${BASE_REF}" "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}"; do
            if [ -n "${tag}" ] && ! [[ "${tag}" =~ ^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$ ]]; then
              echo "::error::unexpected agents-rel tag format: ${tag}" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${BASE_REF}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${BASE_REF}")
          # gh-812: base versions come from what the last release SHIPPED —
          # versions.json on main is a best-effort ledger that can (and did)
          # lag reality by whole releases, re-shipping a live version with
          # new content.
          [ -n "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}" ] && args+=(--prev-release-tag="${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")
          node ci/release_packs.mjs "${args[@]}"
          # Signal "nothing to release" to the publish steps.
          if [ -f dist/.no-release ]; then echo "released=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "released=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

      - name: "Bump versions.json via PR (protection-clean)"
        # Rulesets on personal repos have no bypass actors and no PAT scope
        # can edit them from CI (HTTP 404, live 2026-10-01) — a direct push
        # to main can NEVER satisfy required checks. So the bump rides a
        # side branch + PR + squash merge: quality.yml's crap check
        # satisfies the ruleset. The squash subject carries [skip ci] so the
        # merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not
        # cover versions.json).

        # Nothing-changed guard (gh-690): a server-side auto-merge fires the
        # moment the checks pass and cannot re-verify that main did not move
        # while the PR waited — #689 merged with a 0-byte diff because its
        # branch was cut before the previous ledger PR landed. Instead: skip
        # creating the PR when main already carries the target versions
        # (gu…

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/845
- **Title**: gh-844 [GOAL] Agent-pack release not cut on main merges after 11:25 — fixes sit dead in main (live: #841 sweep 2.75h to live #826 hung)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-844` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +495
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:12:12Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T17:12:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #844
### Root Cause

The agent-pack release has exactly one trigger plane — the GitHub `push` event on main. When the push event for a machine merge is dropped server-side (2026-10-10: #841 at 14:24Z and ~16:00Z #843), nothing detects that main is ahead of the latest `agents-rel-*` tag — fixes sat dead in main 2.75h until an operator dispatch (17:05Z), hanging #826. The failure is silent by construction: no detection, no belt.

### Fix

Belt per the ticket's capability surface, independent of the SM tick engine (which itself rides the release tag and cannot be the only safety net):

- `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release-kicker.yml` — scheduled tick (`*/10 *`, ≤15 min cadence per AC1) + `workflow_dispatch`; compares `origin/main` HEAD vs the newest `agents-rel-*` tag commit, diffs since the tag, counts queued/in-progress release runs, and re-dispatches `agent-pack-release.yml` when main is ahead on non-ignored paths. Concurrency-queued, never cancelled mid-tick.
- `ci/release_kicker_guard.cjs` — pure, unit-tested decision logic (same CJS-guard/ESM-runner split as `pack_release_guard.cjs`). Parses `paths-ignore` **from the release workflow itself** — single source of truth, no hardcoded copy (AC3). `changedFiles: null` and missing-tag both resolve to dispatch — never silently skip.
- `ci/release_kicker.mjs` — thin `gh`/`git` runner executing the guard's decision; every tick logs a `::notice::` decision line (AC1 metric).

The push trigger stays untouched (non-goal). Idempotency (AC2): an in-flight release run suppresses the dispatch, and the release workflow's own ledger guard + `.no-release` no-op dedupe a double dispatch.

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_releaseKicker.js` (new, in `run_all.json`) — 21 tests: paths-ignore parsing/parity, #841 file classification, decideKick states, L2 replay of the 14:24–17:05 gap (dispatches with 4 relevant files), workflow wiring (cadence ≤15 min, `actions: write`, concurrency, dispatch target). RED first (19 failed on missing module), then GREEN.
- Full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`: **2489 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- L3 (live) remains: after merge, the next agents-relevant main merge must cut a release with no operator action — watch the first `Agent Pack Release Kicker` scheduled runs and confirm the `noop — main-already-released` tick lines.
- The webhook-loss theory (why push events were dropped) is still unreconciled; the kicker is the durable fix regardless, per the ticket.
- The kicker needs `actions: write`, granted in the workflow; `GITHUB_TOKEN` `workflow_dispatch` does start runs (not subject to the token-trigger recursion ban).

# gh-844: [GOAL] Agent-pack release not cut on main merges after 11:25 — fixes sit dead in main (live: #841 sweep 2.75h to live; #826 hung)

## Description

## Goal

Agents-side machine fixes become live ONLY when a new agent-pack release is cut (the tick engine rides the latest release tag, not main). The release must be cut on EVERY agents-relevant main merge, reliably — today the push trigger silently skipped two consecutive merges (gh-840 sweep sat in main 2.75h before an operator dispatch; #826 hung the whole time).

## Subject

`.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` push trigger reliability. Timeline 2026-10-10: releases at 07:11 / 07:29 / 08:47 / 09:33 / 09:38 / 09:52 / 11:25 — then SILENCE. Main pushes at 14:24 (#841, files: js/common/reworkConsumption.js, js/smAgent.js, js/unit-tests/*, sm_github.json — all outside paths-ignore .github|docs|site) and ~16:0x (#843) triggered NOTHING. Workflow state=active, file unchanged since 2026-10-09. Operator workflow_dispatch 17:05 cut agents-rel-... manually.

## Capability surface

- Detection: a main merge touching non-ignored paths with NO release run within N minutes → the release is MISSING; alert/dispatch.
- Belt: the SM tick (or a kicker rule) compares latest release tag's commit vs main HEAD each tick; when main is ahead on non-ignored paths and no release run is pending → dispatch workflow_dispatch (idempotent, safe — the workflow computes the affected set itself).
- Optional: reconcile the webhook-loss theory (check GitHub delivery logs) — if push events for machine merges are being dropped, the belt above is the durable fix regardless.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: no agents-side fix waits >15 min in main without a release cut (metric on the board or tick log line).
2. AC2: manual dispatch remains safe/idempotent (no double release for the same content — the version ledger dedupes).
3. AC3: docs/README paths still don't cut releases (paths-ignore preserved).
4. AC4: live — after ship, #841-class fixes activate without operator involvement.

## Test plan

- L1: rule unit tests (main-ahead detection with ignored-path diffs).
- L2: replay the 2026-10-10 14:24-17:05 timeline — the belt would have fired at ~14:39.
- L3 (live): next agents fix merges; release appears without human action.

## Non-goals

- Changing the pack format or compile steps.
- The release workflow's internal steps — only its TRIGGERING reliability.

## References

- Instance: #841 merged 14:24Z; no release until operator dispatch 17:05Z; #826 hung in the gap.
- Context: fa engine pin incident 2026-10-10 (factory_ref) — same "fix merged ≠ live" class.

## Machine jobs

# Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
          # gh-812: the builder reads the previous release's shipped catalog
          # and same-version pack zips (version uniqueness + payload compare).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # gh-812 rework (review thread 3): untrusted tag names reach the
          # script ONLY through env indirection — never template-expanded
          # into the run: block. Actions interpolates ${{ }} BEFORE bash
          # parses the script, so a crafted agents-rel-* tag name (any user
          # with push access can create one; the newest by creatordate wins)
          # could break out of the quoting and run arbitrary code in this
          # contents:write job.
          BASE_REF: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
          PREV_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-812 rework: release-base tags are machine-generated
          # (agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS); anything else in the newest
          # agents-rel-* tag is rejected before it reaches the builder.
          # Empty is allowed — the first release has no base tag.
          for tag in "${BASE_REF}" "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}"; do
            if [ -n "${tag}" ] && ! [[ "${tag}" =~ ^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$ ]]; then
              echo "::error::unexpected agents-rel tag format: ${tag}" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${BASE_REF}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${BASE_REF}")
          # gh-812: base versions come from what the last release SHIPPED —
          # versions.json on main is a best-effort ledger that can (and did)
          # lag reality by whole releases, re-shipping a live version with
          # new content.
          [ -n "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}" ] && args+=(--prev-release-tag="${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")
          node ci/release_packs.mjs "${args[@]}"
          # Signal "nothing to release" to the publish steps.
          if [ -f dist/.no-release ]; then echo "released=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "released=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

      - name: "Bump versions.json via PR (protection-clean)"
        # Rulesets on personal repos have no bypass actors and no PAT scope
        # can edit them from CI (HTTP 404, live 2026-10-01) — a direct push
        # to main can NEVER satisfy required checks. So the bump rides a
        # side branch + PR + squash merge: quality.yml's crap check
        # satisfies the ruleset. The squash subject carries [skip ci] so the
        # merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not
        # cover versions.json).
        #
        # Nothing-changed guard (gh-690): a server-side auto-merge fires the
        # moment the checks pass and cannot re-verify that main did not move
        # while the PR waited — #689 merged with a 0-byte diff because its
        # branch was cut before the previous ledger PR landed. Instead: skip
        # creating the PR when main already carries the target versions
        # (gu…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 845
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/845
- **Title**: gh-844 [GOAL] Agent-pack release not cut on main merges after 11:25 — fixes sit dead in main (live: #841 sweep 2.75h to live #826 hung)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-844` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +495
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:12:12Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T17:12:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #844
### Root Cause

The agent-pack release has exactly one trigger plane — the GitHub `push` event on main. When the push event for a machine merge is dropped server-side (2026-10-10: #841 at 14:24Z and ~16:00Z #843), nothing detects that main is ahead of the latest `agents-rel-*` tag — fixes sat dead in main 2.75h until an operator dispatch (17:05Z), hanging #826. The failure is silent by construction: no detection, no belt.

### Fix

Belt per the ticket's capability surface, independent of the SM tick engine (which itself rides the release tag and cannot be the only safety net):

- `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release-kicker.yml` — scheduled tick (`*/10 *`, ≤15 min cadence per AC1) + `workflow_dispatch`; compares `origin/main` HEAD vs the newest `agents-rel-*` tag commit, diffs since the tag, counts queued/in-progress release runs, and re-dispatches `agent-pack-release.yml` when main is ahead on non-ignored paths. Concurrency-queued, never cancelled mid-tick.
- `ci/release_kicker_guard.cjs` — pure, unit-tested decision logic (same CJS-guard/ESM-runner split as `pack_release_guard.cjs`). Parses `paths-ignore` **from the release workflow itself** — single source of truth, no hardcoded copy (AC3). `changedFiles: null` and missing-tag both resolve to dispatch — never silently skip.
- `ci/release_kicker.mjs` — thin `gh`/`git` runner executing the guard's decision; every tick logs a `::notice::` decision line (AC1 metric).

The push trigger stays untouched (non-goal). Idempotency (AC2): an in-flight release run suppresses the dispatch, and the release workflow's own ledger guard + `.no-release` no-op dedupe a double dispatch.

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_releaseKicker.js` (new, in `run_all.json`) — 21 tests: paths-ignore parsing/parity, #841 file classification, decideKick states, L2 replay of the 14:24–17:05 gap (dispatches with 4 relevant files), workflow wiring (cadence ≤15 min, `actions: write`, concurrency, dispatch target). RED first (19 failed on missing module), then GREEN.
- Full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`: **2489 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- L3 (live) remains: after merge, the next agents-relevant main merge must cut a release with no operator action — watch the first `Agent Pack Release Kicker` scheduled runs and confirm the `noop — main-already-released` tick lines.
- The webhook-loss theory (why push events were dropped) is still unreconciled; the kicker is the durable fix regardless, per the ticket.
- The kicker needs `actions: write`, granted in the workflow; `GITHUB_TOKEN` `workflow_dispatch` does start runs (not subject to the token-trigger recursion ban).

## Description

## Goal

Agents-side machine fixes become live ONLY when a new agent-pack release is cut (the tick engine rides the latest release tag, not main). The release must be cut on EVERY agents-relevant main merge, reliably — today the push trigger silently skipped two consecutive merges (gh-840 sweep sat in main 2.75h before an operator dispatch; #826 hung the whole time).

## Subject

`.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` push trigger reliability. Timeline 2026-10-10: releases at 07:11 / 07:29 / 08:47 / 09:33 / 09:38 / 09:52 / 11:25 — then SILENCE. Main pushes at 14:24 (#841, files: js/common/reworkConsumption.js, js/smAgent.js, js/unit-tests/*, sm_github.json — all outside paths-ignore .github|docs|site) and ~16:0x (#843) triggered NOTHING. Workflow state=active, file unchanged since 2026-10-09. Operator workflow_dispatch 17:05 cut agents-rel-... manually.

## Capability surface

- Detection: a main merge touching non-ignored paths with NO release run within N minutes → the release is MISSING; alert/dispatch.
- Belt: the SM tick (or a kicker rule) compares latest release tag's commit vs main HEAD each tick; when main is ahead on non-ignored paths and no release run is pending → dispatch workflow_dispatch (idempotent, safe — the workflow computes the affected set itself).
- Optional: reconcile the webhook-loss theory (check GitHub delivery logs) — if push events for machine merges are being dropped, the belt above is the durable fix regardless.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: no agents-side fix waits >15 min in main without a release cut (metric on the board or tick log line).
2. AC2: manual dispatch remains safe/idempotent (no double release for the same content — the version ledger dedupes).
3. AC3: docs/README paths still don't cut releases (paths-ignore preserved).
4. AC4: live — after ship, #841-class fixes activate without operator involvement.

## Test plan

- L1: rule unit tests (main-ahead detection with ignored-path diffs).
- L2: replay the 2026-10-10 14:24-17:05 timeline — the belt would have fired at ~14:39.
- L3 (live): next agents fix merges; release appears without human action.

## Non-goals

- Changing the pack format or compile steps.
- The release workflow's internal steps — only its TRIGGERING reliability.

## References

- Instance: #841 merged 14:24Z; no release until operator dispatch 17:05Z; #826 hung in the gap.

# Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
          # gh-812: the builder reads the previous release's shipped catalog
          # and same-version pack zips (version uniqueness + payload compare).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # gh-812 rework (review thread 3): untrusted tag names reach the
          # script ONLY through env indirection — never template-expanded
          # into the run: block. Actions interpolates ${{ }} BEFORE bash
          # parses the script, so a crafted agents-rel-* tag name (any user
          # with push access can create one; the newest by creatordate wins)
          # could break out of the quoting and run arbitrary code in this
          # contents:write job.
          BASE_REF: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
          PREV_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-812 rework: release-base tags are machine-generated
          # (agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS); anything else in the newest
          # agents-rel-* tag is rejected before it reaches the builder.
          # Empty is allowed — the first release has no base tag.
          for tag in "${BASE_REF}" "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}"; do
            if [ -n "${tag}" ] && ! [[ "${tag}" =~ ^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$ ]]; then
              echo "::error::unexpected agents-rel tag format: ${tag}" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${BASE_REF}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${BASE_REF}")
          # gh-812: base versions come from what the last release SHIPPED —
          # versions.json on main is a best-effort ledger that can (and did)
          # lag reality by whole releases, re-shipping a live version with
          # new content.
          [ -n "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}" ] && args+=(--prev-release-tag="${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")
          node ci/release_packs.mjs "${args[@]}"
          # Signal "nothing to release" to the publish steps.
          if [ -f dist/.no-release ]; then echo "released=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "released=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

      - name: "Bump versions.json via PR (protection-clean)"
        # Rulesets on personal repos have no bypass actors and no PAT scope
        # can edit them from CI (HTTP 404, live 2026-10-01) — a direct push
        # to main can NEVER satisfy required checks. So the bump rides a
        # side branch + PR + squash merge: quality.yml's crap check
        # satisfies the ruleset. The squash subject carries [skip ci] so the
        # merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not
        # cover versions.json).
        #
        # Nothing-changed guard (gh-690): a server-side auto-merge fires the
        # moment the checks pass and cannot re-verify that main did not move
        # while the PR waited — #689 merged with a 0-byte diff because its
        # branch was cut before the previous ledger PR landed. Instead: skip
        # creating the PR when main already carries the target versions
        # (gu…

   a. `git diff --name-only ${releaseCommit}...${mainHead}` — three-dot diff uses merge-base of the two. Since tags are on main history, merge-base(tag, mainHead) = tag commit (if tag is ancestor of main). Fine. But if tag is NOT ancestor (e.g., tag created on a release commit pushed to main — the release workflow creates the tag via gh release create, and commits versions.json to main... the tag points at the main HEAD at release time presumably). Fine.

Actually default `--limit` is 10 for `gh run list`. If more than 10 recent runs exist... The kicker repo probably has fewer runs. But the release workflow runs on each merge; over time there could be many. The filter counts queued/in_progress among the most recent 10 runs. If 10 runs all completed and an 11th is queued... unlikely scenario but `gh run list` default limit is 10. Hmm, but the query would return the 10 most recent runs; if one is queued it would be within the 10 most recent since it's most recent by created date. Qued/in-progress runs are the newest, so they'd always be within the recent window. Only pathological if more than 10 runs were created while one sits queued. Marginal. Could suggest passing `--limit` higher or filtering. Minor/suggestion.

But the PR description says release workflow's ledger guard + .no-release no-op dedupe a double dispatch, and release workflow has concurrency group `agent-pack-release` with cancel-in-progress: false, so double dispatch → second run no-ops. Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 845
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/845
- **Title**: gh-844 [GOAL] Agent-pack release not cut on main merges after 11:25 — fixes sit dead in main (live: #841 sweep 2.75h to live #826 hung)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-844` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +495
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:12:12Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T17:12:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #844
### Root Cause

The agent-pack release has exactly one trigger plane — the GitHub `push` event on main. When the push event for a machine merge is dropped server-side (2026-10-10: #841 at 14:24Z and ~16:00Z #843), nothing detects that main is ahead of the latest `agents-rel-*` tag — fixes sat dead in main 2.75h until an operator dispatch (17:05Z), hanging #826. The failure is silent by construction: no detection, no belt.

### Fix

Belt per the ticket's capability surface, independent of the SM tick engine (which itself rides the release tag and cannot be the only safety net):

- `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release-kicker.yml` — scheduled tick (`*/10 *`, ≤15 min cadence per AC1) + `workflow_dispatch`; compares `origin/main` HEAD vs the newest `agents-rel-*` tag commit, diffs since the tag, counts queued/in-progress release runs, and re-dispatches `agent-pack-release.yml` when main is ahead on non-ignored paths. Concurrency-queued, never cancelled mid-tick.
- `ci/release_kicker_guard.cjs` — pure, unit-tested decision logic (same CJS-guard/ESM-runner split as `pack_release_guard.cjs`). Parses `paths-ignore` **from the release workflow itself** — single source of truth, no hardcoded copy (AC3). `changedFiles: null` and missing-tag both resolve to dispatch — never silently skip.
- `ci/release_kicker.mjs` — thin `gh`/`git` runner executing the guard's decision; every tick logs a `::notice::` decision line (AC1 metric).

The push trigger stays untouched (non-goal). Idempotency (AC2): an in-flight release run suppresses the dispatch, and the release workflow's own ledger guard + `.no-release` no-op dedupe a double dispatch.

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_releaseKicker.js` (new, in `run_all.json`) — 21 tests: paths-ignore parsing/parity, #841 file classification, decideKick states, L2 replay of the 14:24–17:05 gap (dispatches with 4 relevant files), workflow wiring (cadence ≤15 min, `actions: write`, concurrency, dispatch target). RED first (19 failed on missing module), then GREEN.
- Full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`: **2489 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- L3 (live) remains: after merge, the next agents-relevant main merge must cut a release with no operator action — watch the first `Agent Pack Release Kicker` scheduled runs and confirm the `noop — main-already-released` tick lines.
- The webhook-loss theory (why push events were dropped) is still unreconciled; the kicker is the durable fix regardless, per the ticket.
- The kicker needs `actions: write`, granted in the workflow; `GITHUB_TOKEN` `workflow_dispatch` does start runs (not subject to the token-trigger recursion ban).

## Description

## Goal

Agents-side machine fixes become live ONLY when a new agent-pack release is cut (the tick engine rides the latest release tag, not main). The release must be cut on EVERY agents-relevant main merge, reliably — today the push trigger silently skipped two consecutive merges (gh-840 sweep sat in main 2.75h before an operator dispatch; #826 hung the whole time).

## Subject

`.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` push trigger reliability. Timeline 2026-10-10: releases at 07:11 / 07:29 / 08:47 / 09:33 / 09:38 / 09:52 / 11:25 — then SILENCE. ## Capability surface

# Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
          # gh-812: the builder reads the previous release's shipped catalog
          # and same-version pack zips (version uniqueness + payload compare).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # gh-812 rework (review thread 3): untrusted tag names reach the
          # script ONLY through env indirection — never template-expanded
          # into the run: block. Actions interpolates ${{ }} BEFORE bash
          # parses the script, so a crafted agents-rel-* tag name (any user
          # with push access can create one; the newest by creatordate wins)
          # could break out of the quoting and run arbitrary code in this
          # contents:write job.
          BASE_REF: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
          PREV_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-812 rework: release-base tags are machine-generated
          # (agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS); anything else in the newest
          # agents-rel-* tag is rejected before it reaches the builder.
          # Empty is allowed — the first release has no base tag.
          for tag in "${BASE_REF}" "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}"; do
            if [ -n "${tag}" ] && ! [[ "${tag}" =~ ^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$ ]]; then
              echo "::error::unexpected agents-rel tag format: ${tag}" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${BASE_REF}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${BASE_REF}")

          # versions.json on main is a best-effort ledger that can (and did)
          # lag reality by whole releases, re-shipping a live version with
          # new content.

          if [ -f dist/.no-release ]; then echo "released=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "released=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 845
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/845
- **Title**: gh-844 [GOAL] Agent-pack release not cut on main merges after 11:25 — fixes sit dead in main (live: #841 sweep 2.75h to live #826 hung)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-844` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +495
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:12:12Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T17:12:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #844
### Root Cause

The agent-pack release has exactly one trigger plane — the GitHub `push` event on main. When the push event for a machine merge is dropped server-side (2026-10-10: #841 at 14:24Z and ~16:00Z #843), nothing detects that main is ahead of the latest `agents-rel-*` tag — fixes sat dead in main 2.75h until an operator dispatch (17:05Z), hanging #826. The failure is silent by construction: no detection, no belt.

### Fix

Belt per the ticket's capability surface, independent of the SM tick engine (which itself rides the release tag and cannot be the only safety net):

- `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release-kicker.yml` — scheduled tick (`*/10 *`, ≤15 min cadence per AC1) + `workflow_dispatch`; compares `origin/main` HEAD vs the newest `agents-rel-*` tag commit, diffs since the tag, counts queued/in-progress release runs, and re-dispatches `agent-pack-release.yml` when main is ahead on non-ignored paths. Concurrency-queued, never cancelled mid-tick.
- `ci/release_kicker_guard.cjs` — pure, unit-tested decision logic (same CJS-guard/ESM-runner split as `pack_release_guard.cjs`). Parses `paths-ignore` **from the release workflow itself** — single source of truth, no hardcoded copy (AC3). `changedFiles: null` and missing-tag both resolve to dispatch — never silently skip.
- `ci/release_kicker.mjs` — thin `gh`/`git` runner executing the guard's decision; every tick logs a `::notice::` decision line (AC1 metric).

The push trigger stays untouched (non-goal). Idempotency (AC2): an in-flight release run suppresses the dispatch, and the release workflow's own ledger guard + `.no-release` no-op dedupe a double dispatch.

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_releaseKicker.js` (new, in `run_all.json`) — 21 tests: paths-ignore parsing/parity, #841 file classification, decideKick states, L2 replay of the 14:24–17:05 gap (dispatches with 4 relevant files), workflow wiring (cadence ≤15 min, `actions: write`, concurrency, dispatch target). RED first (19 failed on missing module), then GREEN.
- Full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`: **2489 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- L3 (live) remains: after merge, the next agents-relevant main merge must cut a release with no operator action — watch the first `Agent Pack Release Kicker` scheduled runs and confirm the `noop — main-already-released` tick lines.
- The webhook-loss theory (why push events were dropped) is still unreconciled; the kicker is the durable fix regardless, per the ticket.
- The kicker needs `actions: write`, granted in the workflow; `GITHUB_TOKEN` `workflow_dispatch` does start runs (not subject to the token-trigger recursion ban).

## Description

## Goal

Agents-side machine fixes become live ONLY when a new agent-pack release is cut (the tick engine rides the latest release tag, not main). The release must be cut on EVERY agents-relevant main merge, reliably — today the push trigger silently skipped two consecutive merges (gh-840 sweep sat in main 2.75h before an operator dispatch; #826 hung the whole time).

## Subject

## Capability surface

# Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.

          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

          PREV_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}

- **Author**: ai-teammate

- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:12:12Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T17:12:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #844
### Root Cause

The agent-pack release has exactly one trigger plane — the GitHub `push` event on main. When the push event for a machine merge is dropped server-side (2026-10-10: #841 at 14:24Z and ~16:00Z #843), nothing detects that main is ahead of the latest `agents-rel-*` tag — fixes sat dead in main 2.75h until an operator dispatch (17:05Z), hanging #826. The failure is silent by construction: no detection, no belt.

### Fix

Belt per the ticket's capability surface, independent of the SM tick engine (which itself rides the release tag and cannot be the only safety net):

- `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release-kicker.yml` — scheduled tick (`*/10 *`, ≤15 min cadence per AC1) + `workflow_dispatch`; compares `origin/main` HEAD vs the newest `agents-rel-*` tag commit, diffs since the tag, counts queued/in-progress release runs, and re-dispatches `agent-pack-release.yml` when main is ahead on non-ignored paths. Concurrency-queued, never cancelled mid-tick.
- `ci/release_kicker_guard.cjs` — pure, unit-tested decision logic (same CJS-guard/ESM-runner split as `pack_release_guard.cjs`). Parses `paths-ignore` **from the release workflow itself** — single source of truth, no hardcoded copy (AC3). `changedFiles: null` and missing-tag both resolve to dispatch — never silently skip.
- `ci/release_kicker.mjs` — thin `gh`/`git` runner executing the guard's decision; every tick logs a `::notice::` decision line (AC1 metric).

The push trigger stays untouched (non-goal). Idempotency (AC2): an in-flight release run suppresses the dispatch, and the release workflow's own ledger guard + `.no-release` no-op dedupe a double dispatch.

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_releaseKicker.js` (new, in `run_all.json`) — 21 tests: paths-ignore parsing/parity, #841 file classification, decideKick states, L2 replay of the 14:24–17:05 gap (dispatches with 4 relevant files), workflow wiring (cadence ≤15 min, `actions: write`, concurrency, dispatch target). RED first (19 failed on missing module), then GREEN.
- Full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`: **2489 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- L3 (live) remains: after merge, the next agents-relevant main merge must cut a release with no operator action — watch the first `Agent Pack Release Kicker` scheduled runs and confirm the `noop — main-already-released` tick lines.
- The webhook-loss theory (why push events were dropped) is still unreconciled; the kicker is the durable fix regardless, per the ticket.
- The kicker needs `actions: write`, granted in the workflow; `GITHUB_TOKEN` `workflow_dispatch` does start runs (not subject to the token-trigger recursion ban).
